newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission set to propose ban on suspect sheep tissue.
newsitem.headline: Commission set to propose ban on suspect sheep tissue.

text.p: The European Commission is expected to finalise on Tuesday a proposal to ban suspect tissue from sheep and goats, as well as cattle, at risk to scrapie or mad cow disease, Commission officials said.
The proposal, which was overwhelmingly rejected last week by the Standing Veterinary Committee, is due to be adopted without discussion at the Commission's weekly meeting in Strasbourg.
It will be sent to the Farm Council on December 16-17.
The proposal is a precautionary move to protect public health after British and French research showed that sheep could catch mad cow disease, or Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE).
It calls for the removal of the brains, eyes, spinal cord and spleen from sheep, goats and cattle over 12 months old and its exclusion from human and animal food.
Sheep have for centuries been known to suffer from scrapie, a brain-wasting disease similar to BSE, which can be passed from one animal to another and from ewe to lamb but not to humans.

Last week, only British and French veterinary officials supported the proposal, while Ireland abstained. Other countries voted against, saying they were virtually BSE-free and the measures were economically unjustified.
Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler has rejected that argument, saying member states must do everything possible to minimise the health risk and restore consumer confidence.
However, officials said the proposal was unlikely to gain the necessary simple majority -- support of eight farm ministers -- next week.
The Commission has resisted attempts by BSE-free member states to be exempted from the measures, saying none are totally risk free and such a move would distort meat trade in the EU single market.
But exemptions may be granted non-EU countries which satisfy the Commission about the safety of their meat.
This could help unblock negotiations with the United States on the mutual recognition of veterinary standards. The two sides have been at odds over U.S. exports of petfood containing sheep tissue.
